lesson.1_1.title: Income, expenses, needs and wants
lesson.1_1.gut.prompt: It's Month 1. Your family covers food, school fees and travel. You have ₹2,000 to use however you like. A pair of sneakers you love costs ₹1,800. What do you do?
lesson.1_1.gut.a.label: Buy the sneakers
lesson.1_1.gut.a.result: You have the sneakers and ₹200 left. Next month a friend asks you to a movie: you have ₹200. Joy now, but little room for anything else.
lesson.1_1.gut.b.label: Save all ₹2,000
lesson.1_1.gut.b.result: You have ₹2,000 saved. Nothing to spend on a friend's movie, and no new shoes. Safe, but a little dull.
lesson.1_1.gut.c.label: Split: ₹1,200 save, ₹800 spend
lesson.1_1.gut.c.result: You can enjoy something small and still grow your savings. Nice balance.
lesson.1_1.gut.bridge: There's no single right answer. Let's learn the words that help you decide.
lesson.1_1.c1.text: Money comes in. Money goes out. Where does yours go?
lesson.1_1.c2.text: Income is money that comes to you. Pocket money, a gift, a part-time job, a scholarship.
lesson.1_1.c3.text: An expense is money you spend. Some come every month, like a phone recharge. Some come now and then, like a birthday gift.
lesson.1_1.c4.text: Fixed expenses stay the same: bus pass, tuition fee. Variable expenses change: snacks, outings.
lesson.1_1.c4.reveal.prompt: Which one can you change more easily?
lesson.1_1.c4.reveal.answer: Variable expenses. You choose how many snacks and outings.
lesson.1_1.c5.text: A need is something you must have to live and study. A want is something that makes life nicer, but you can live without it.
lesson.1_1.c6.text: Some things are in between. A phone for studying is a need. An ₹80,000 phone is more of a want. Ask: "What happens if I don't buy this?"
lesson.1_1.c6.sort.prompt: Sort each one: need or want?
lesson.1_1.c6.sort.feedback: Needs keep you living and studying. Wants make life nicer. Both are fine; wants just need a plan.
lesson.1_1.c7.text: In Capito, your needs are already covered by your family or by you. The money you earn here is only for wants and savings.
lesson.1_1.c7.footer: Wants are not bad. They just need a plan.
lesson.1_1.c8.text: ₹40 a day on snacks sounds small. In a year it's ₹14,600.
lesson.1_1.q1.prompt: Which of these is a want?
lesson.1_1.q1.right: Yes. The skin is nice, but you can live without it. That makes it a want.
lesson.1_1.q1.wrong: Fees, rice and a bus pass are things you need to live and study. The skin is nice, but you can live without it.
lesson.1_1.q2.prompt: You spend ₹40 on snacks every day. About how much is that in a year?
lesson.1_1.q2.right: Right: ₹40 × 365 days = ₹14,600. Small spends add up.
lesson.1_1.q2.wrong: Multiply ₹40 by 365 days. Small spends add up to ₹14,600.
lesson.1_1.q3.prompt: Spending on wants is always a bad thing.
lesson.1_1.q3.right: Correct, it's false. Wants are part of a good life. The skill is planning for them.
lesson.1_1.q3.wrong: It's false. Wants are part of a good life. The skill is planning for them, so they don't crowd out your savings.
lesson.1_1.effect: Your Month 1 money lands in your Wallet, and you add your first want to My Wants.
